Normandie poster by Cassandre

Cassandre’s poster for the French Line shows the liner Normandie head-on: a looming, symmetrical black hull above a band of sea and a stack of centered capitals.

Source
Victoria and Albert Museum: Normandie, E.648-2017
Creator
Cassandre (Adolphe Mouron)
Made
1935
Style
Art Deco (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Monumental, optimistic, streamlined
Evidence
Downloaded the V&A image (580 × 900 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. Read the V&A record through its API. The MoMA record could not be read: HTTP 403 to WebFetch, and Claude in Chrome had no permission for moma.org. No image is stored.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A calls the poster “arguably the most iconic work of Cassandre (1901–68)” and says the Normandie entered service with the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique in 1935 and was conceived as a showcase of French Art Deco design. It notes the simplicity and symmetry of the frontal view. V&A.

The V&A records colour lithograph on paper backed on cotton, 100.5 × 62.5 cm, printed by Alliance Graphique L. Danel, Paris, 1935. V&A.

Observed

  • The bow of the ship fills the upper two-thirds, seen from straight ahead and below, so the hull narrows to a vertical center line.
  • The hull is black and gray with a red band at the waterline; white superstructure decks flare out on both sides near the top, and a red and black funnel sits above.
  • The sky is a gradient from deep blue at top to pale blue; a small flock of white birds crosses the lower hull.
  • A green band of sea runs across below the hull.
  • “NORMANDIE” is centered in large white sans-serif capitals, followed by centered lines in black and red capitals giving the line and the route Le Havre – Southampton – New-York.
  • The signature “A.M. CASSANDRE” is at upper right. The composition is symmetrical about the bow.

Why it belongs

The poster uses Deco symmetry and a stepped, flaring silhouette, but its smooth gradients and machine subject point to the streamline branch the style record lists as a close relative.

The low viewpoint makes the object monumental, the same device as a setback tower seen from the street.

Borrow

Center one monumental object on the vertical axis and let it narrow toward the viewer.

Stack centered lines of capitals under the image, changing only color between lines.
